configuration.title: Proxy Toggler
capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.descrip: In Restricted Mode, a folder's settings cannot set proxyToggler.defaultProfile.
configuration.defaultProfile.description: The proxy profile to turn on, by name, when a window of this project gains focus, or `false` for no proxy. Set it in a project's settings for that project, or in your user settings for every project that sets none; leave it unset to switch only by hand. A change made in a window lasts until that window closes or reloads. Set it from the switcher's **This Project** entries.
configuration.applyToTerminals.descripti: Give new integrated terminals and tasks the proxy VS Code uses, as `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` in upper and lower case, so that Git, npm and other command-line tools use it too. Read only from user settings. Terminals already open need a relaunch.
configuration.confirmBeforeToggle.descri: Ask before the status bar toggle or the Toggle Proxy command turns the proxy on or off.
configuration.profiles.description: Proxy profiles the status bar toggle switches between. Shared by every VS Code Profile and read only from user settings: edit them with **Preferences: Open Application Settings (JSON)**. Profiles hold no credentials; VS Code asks for a proxy sign-in itself.
configuration.profiles.name.description: The profile name, unique ignoring letter case and at most 30 characters.
configuration.profiles.proxyUrl.descript: The proxy URL with its port, such as http://proxy.example.com:8080 or socks5://proxy.example.com:1080, without a user name or password. socks4, socks4a and socks5h are not supported.
configuration.profiles.strictSSL.descrip: The value for http.proxyStrictSSL. Only VS Code's command line and some built-in extensions honor it.
configuration.profiles.bypassList.descri: Hosts that VS Code reaches directly, written to http.noProxy: host names, IP addresses, or domains that start with a dot, such as .example.com.
command.switchProfile.title: Proxy Toggler: Switch Profile…
configuration.showSwitchNotifications.de: Show a short notification, naming the profile, when the proxy turns on or off or switches profiles. The status bar always shows the result.
walkthrough.title: Get Started with Proxy Toggler
walkthrough.description: Add your proxy, turn it on and off from the status bar, and give terminals and projects the proxy they need.
walkthrough.addProfile.title: Add your proxy
walkthrough.addProfile.description:
A profile is a proxy with a name, such as Work or Home. Enter the proxy URL, then the name. If VS Code already uses a proxy, setup starts from it.
[Configure Proxy Settings](command:proxyToggler.configure)
walkthrough.toggle.title: Turn the proxy on and off
walkthrough.toggle.description:
Click **Proxy** in the status bar to turn the current profile on, or the proxy off. The status bar shows which profile is in use.
[Toggle Proxy](command:proxyToggler.toggle)
walkthrough.switchProfile.title: Switch profiles
walkthrough.switchProfile.description:
Click the gear next to the toggle and pick a profile to turn it on. The switcher also adds, edits and deletes profiles, and **Edit Profile…** tests a connection through one.
[Switch Profile](command:proxyToggler.switchProfile)
walkthrough.terminals.title: Use the proxy in terminals
walkthrough.terminals.description:
VS Code's proxy does not reach its integrated terminals. Turn on **Apply To Terminals** in your user settings, and new terminals and tasks get it as `http_proxy`, `https_proxy` and `no_proxy`, which Git, npm and curl read.
[Open the Setting](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22proxyToggler.applyToTerminals%22%5D)
walkthrough.projectDefault.title: Give a project its own proxy
walkthrough.projectDefault.description:
A project can name the profile it uses, and VS Code's proxy follows the window you work in. With a folder open, turn on the profile the project needs, then pick **Use … in This Project** in the switcher.
[Switch Profile](command:proxyToggler.switchProfile)
